original.title: Check thermal and dissipative consistency
original.qualification: For the warm or damped branches, test the stated dissipation law, thermal dominance and required strength independently of observational agreement. Thermal trapping remains a separate mechanism; thermal perturbations provide no automatic TCC exemption, and later-stage relaxation differs from imposing TCC throughout.
original.reason: c11's conditional viability question requires model-specific thermal consistency, which c1 explicitly investigates and u25 makes an independent test.

judgment.reason: The premise-check direction is useful, but applying thermal-dominance checks to 'warm or damped branches' can transfer a thermal premise to unspecified additional damping. c11 and u11 do not license that universal requirement. Replace with cn0, which checks thermal dominance and dissipation strength only when invoked by the model.

navigation.title: Check the model's thermal and dissipative assumptions
navigation.qualification: For a warm or dissipative scenario, check the consistency conditions its mechanism actually invokes. Test thermal dominance or a specified dissipation strength only where assumed; additional damping alone establishes neither requirement. Thermal trapping remains a distinct mechanism. Thermal perturbations provide no automatic TCC exemption, and relaxing TCC for later stages differs from imposing it throughout.
navigation.reason: c1 provides model-specific consistency questions relevant to c11's conditional viability tests. The tachyon and RS-II witnesses illustrate such checks without exporting their thermal or strong-dissipation premises to every c11 model.
